claims.text: MODULE-WIDE, closing the limitation named in CHECKPOINT-36: across all 32 source files on ARM-08's branch, every write to a protected counter falls into exactly three categories and none is a bypass. One write on the gated skill path (RxSkillSystem.cpp:429, gate at 355); 30 in the boss FSM, which is authority moving its own state and is what authority means; 25 in URxSkillGateCommandlet, which constructs LOCAL FRxSimWorld fixtures and is invoked explicitly via Main() rather than reachable from play.

The scan flagged a third category and I adjudicated it rather than reporting a bypass. RxSkillGateCommandlet is ARM-08's own gate-verification harness — header intent 'exercises the E11 write-scope gate through the REAL FString path' — writing fixture values into a local world it constructed. My own worktree's RxOracleCommandlet uses the identical pattern, so fixture-setup inside a verification commandlet is established practice here. Reporting it as an authority bypass would have been a false alarm against another arm's correct work.

Incidental finding for my own arm, from ARM-08's header: 'RxOracleCommandlet exits 1 even on PASS because of pre-existing GameFeatureData...'. That is the commandlet my task-1 report described as not runnable in this worktree. If it is ever built here, its exit code is not a trustworthy pass/fail signal without accounting for that. Recorded, not verified — I have not built it.

tests.command: materialise 32 .cpp/.h from arm/e11-authority-impl-v1; scan every file for writes to the five protected counter fields; classify each site

decisions_requested: K-01C static half is now complete: registry corresponds to spec (CHECKPOINT-35), no unguarded write on the admission path (CHECKPOINT-36), and no bypass anywhere in the module (this one). The behavioural half needs a built editor — and ARM-08 ships RxSkillGateCommandlet precisely to exercise it, which is the natural instrument for K-01C's remainder.
risks: I classified the commandlet as non-product by reading its type, entry point and fixture construction. I did not verify it is excluded from a shipping build. A commandlet that ships and can be invoked is a different risk profile than one stripped at packaging, and I have not checked the target rules.

The scan matches writes by regex across 32 files. It found 56 sites including the one real gated write, which is its positive control, but a write expressed through a reference or helper would still evade it.
